transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. tell me your dream, however it comes back to you.
Oh hey. The main thing I remember is being on this streetcar, watching the guy driving it.
oh, watching him, not the street. what was he like?
Just a conductor doing his job, nothing special. But there was this lever he turned whenever we went around a bend. I started to feel like I was driving with him.
that's a strange thing to feel. what made the lever so interesting to you?
I don’t know, it just kept catching my eye. When we hit a sharp corner, I’d go through the motions of turning it myself, like I was steering the car.
almost like your hand knew what to do even though you weren't the one driving.
Yeah, exactly. It felt natural, like I was part of it. Then the next thing I knew, I was on top of the car, and it had turned into a train.
wait, on top of it? and it changed into a train mid-dream like that?
Yeah, suddenly I was up on the roof. It was really high up and going fast. I kept almost falling off.
that sounds scary. how did you hold on?
I don’t remember exactly. I was just gripping whatever I could, but it still felt like I might slip. Especially when the train rounded a bend.
bends again. so even up there, the turning was the dangerous part.
Yeah, and I was afraid I’d try to jump off. Most of all at the bends. I was really scared.
scared you'd jump, not just fall. that's different. what made you think you might?
I don’t know. It was so high and moving so fast, and the fear made me feel like I might do something stupid. I just kept thinking about jumping off when we turned.
like the fear itself was pulling you toward the edge.
Exactly. It was like the fear wanted me to jump. Then I noticed another family was sitting on top of the train with me.
who were they?
I don’t remember who they were, just a family. There was a small baby with them, and it seemed thrilled, like it was having fun.
a baby, thrilled, while you're terrified up there. that contrast is something.
Yeah, it made me feel like I was the only one afraid. Everyone else seemed fine on that train, even the baby.
that can feel lonely. did anything happen after you saw them?
Not really. The train was on a country road, and that’s the last thing I remember.
on the streetcar, on the train — it was you, not someone else?
Yeah, it was me the whole time. Even when I felt like I was driving with the conductor, I was still just watching from where I was.
so you never actually took the controls, you only imagined your hand doing it.
Right, I never touched the lever. It just felt like I was going through the same motions in my head.
if you had to pick the one moment from this dream you'd pause and sit inside for a second, which moment would it be?
When the train was rounding a bend and I was sure I’d fall. That feeling of being up so high, going fast, and just holding on.
that moment, at the bend, up high. how did the world around you look in that instant?
Everything was kind of a blur below, like the fields and road were rushing past. It was really high up, I just remember that part.
a blur below, and high up. what kind of light was it?
I don’t really remember, maybe just daytime. Nothing special.
fair enough. and could you hear anything in that moment?
I don’t remember much sound. Maybe the train moving, but that’s all.

so you were on a streetcar, watching the conductor turn this lever on the bends, and it felt natural, like your hand was doing it too even though you never touched it. then suddenly you were on top of the car, and it had become a train, high up and going fast. you were holding on, scared you might slip, and at the bends the fear made you think about jumping off. there was a family up there too, with a small baby who seemed thrilled, and that made you feel like the only one afraid. the last thing you remember is the train on a country road. the moment that stayed with you was rounding a bend, sure you'd fall, up high with everything a blur below in the daytime, maybe the sound of the train moving.

did i get that right? or did i miss anything?
Yeah, you got it right. That’s pretty much exactly it.
would you like me to draw it for you?
Yeah, that would be cool.

there are a few ways i could draw it for you. rough charcoal with white highlights — fast and smeared, kind of like the rush of the train. or thick, carved shapes so the train looks like a simple solid toy. or loose watercolour, where the train's lines curve and everything below goes soft. or a faded photograph, like a memory, with even light and a little grain.

which feels closest to your dream? or would you rather describe your own way?
The rough charcoal one feels closest. Like the rush and blur I felt.

i'll start with the train top. i picture it high up, the roof of a train moving fast on a country road. below, the road and fields blur past from the speed. for the light, daytime is my guess.

does any of that feel off, or should i just leave it to me?
That feels right. Go with your guess.

i'm sketching the train top and the conductor and the family and the streetcar and the streetcar top and the lever now — it'll appear on the right. only that, nothing else is being drawn yet.

as you are — you can tell me a little about yourself — or however i imagine you?
I’m just a normal person, I guess. Nothing too exciting. You can imagine me however you want.
i'll imagine you then — just you, up on that train, holding on.
Oh, it looks right. I’m up there holding on, just like that.
does it look the way you remember it?
Yeah, it does. Especially the blur below and being high up. That part feels right.

i'll draw it for you now, with the train top and you holding on, and the road and fields turning to a blur below. i'll mark the blur and the height and the speed and the way you're holding on as done once i add each part.

tell me if anything in what appears feels wrong, and i'll change it.
It looks right to me. The speed and the height are there.

good, i'll keep it that way.

i'm glad the speed and height feel true to it. the rest of the drawing will fill in soon.
Okay, cool. I’m excited to see the rest.
i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each carrying on from the ones before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
Alright, sounds good.
the moment where you sat in the streetcar, watching the conductor turn that lever on the bends, is up now. does it look the way you remember it?
Yeah, that looks right. Me watching him and the lever on the bend.

i'm glad it feels right to you.

the other moments are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
Okay, no rush.
the conductor turning the lever as the streetcar rounds is up now. does that look the way you remember it?
